title: Ultrasound Lets Scientists Check Coral Without Harming It
summary:
Coral can now get a health check without being hurt. Scientists used an ultrasound machine, the same kind doctors use to look inside the human body, to look inside living coral under water and spot eggs growing within it. It is the first time they can check a coral's health without cutting it open.

Until now, checking for eggs usually meant cutting the coral open. The new way uses sound waves instead. Canon, the camera company, said this week that its medical ultrasound machine, the Aplio i700, can scan coral under water. With the group Coral Spawning International, the team scanned six kinds of large polyp stony coral and saw through their hard skeletons.

To be sure the scans were right, the team cut open one kind of coral, Trachyphyllia geoffroyi, and took close-up pictures of its inside. The pictures matched the scans, showing the shapes were really eggs.

Knowing when corals will release their eggs can help people who protect reefs plan their work and give breeding programs a head start. Coral needs help: late last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned that 96 percent of Earth's coral reef systems face a very high risk of collapse within the next 50 years.
why_it_matters: Healthy coral reefs keep ocean animals alive and keep the sea beautiful for children to visit, explore, and learn about.
